So, lately, the action starts around 7PM. It's mostly clear blue sky until about 7PM or so, and then the clouds start rolling in like clockwork. Mostly scattered rain clouds with occasional thunder and lightening. The clouds move in from the west, yet the wind shifts from the south to mostly north. Precipitation is hit or miss. Stand 100 feet this way or that way, is the difference between zero, Trace, or 0.01 inches of rain.

It is a welcome relief from the relentless weeks of deadly 100+ degrees F of heat. It's now safe to spend more time outdoors during the day. Everything has to be done in the very early hours before the brutal sun releases more heat. 

It was 54F this morning with no wind. We have been enduring temperature swings of 50F in the morning to over 100F into the late afternoons. What little moisture we get lately, has been just enough to turn some of the prairie grass from brown to green.

We have had very few insects this summer. The fewest grasshoppers and mosquitoes I can recall for the past 20 years of living. I suspect the drought has taken it's toll on insects and the birds that normally feed on them. We have had no Tree Swallows this summer thanks to the heat. Our latitude is especially brutal on these birds during the summer, and the heat has splintered all my birding boxes.  

We are now seeing the day temperature trending into the 80s. The race is now on to finish gardening, yard maintenance, and house repairs before the winter sets in. Fall (like spring) is way too short. It's mostly winter or summer here.

However, I am grateful that we have experienced little hail stones, no flooding, no hurricanes, tornadoes, or monster dust devils that rip off roofs or tear off wall sidings. 

We continue to plant trees to replace the ones killed by the drought and look forward to better, milder weather as we continue our trip around the sun.
